original_sentence: Friendship on the rocks: please advise!
readingExamples: Friendship on the rocks: please advise!
definitionEn:
(1) phr. (of a relationship, marriage or business) experiencing serious difficulties and likely to fail or collapse soon
(2) phr. (of a ship) run aground on rocks and wrecked
(3) phr. (of a drink, especially whisky) served with ice cubes but without water

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (酒)加冰块的(常见于餐饮场景,如 whisky on the rocks)
uncommonMeanings.example: The old sailor sat alone at the bar, a whisky on the rocks melting slowly in front of him, his weathered eyes fixed on a photograph no one else could see. （读后续写·人物刻画·孤独氛围）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (船)触礁搁浅;失事
uncommonMeanings.example: By dawn the fishing boat lay on the rocks, its hull torn open by the reef, yet the whole crew had somehow made it ashore alive. （读后续写·海难脱险·环境描写）

posExamples.sentence: Ever since the misunderstanding over the borrowed diary, our once-inseparable friendship had been on the rocks, and every awkward silence in class reminded me of what we had lost. （读后续写·友谊裂痕·心理描写）
I am writing to seek your advice because my friendship with my closest classmate seems to be on the rocks, and I have no idea how to mend the growing distance between us. （应用文·求助信）
When a relationship appears to be on the rocks, running away is never the answer; only honest communication and a willingness to forgive can steer it back to calmer waters. （议论文·人际交往·比喻论证）
The small family bookshop had been on the rocks for months, yet the moment neighbours heard the news, they rushed in to buy, determined not to let a piece of their childhood disappear. （读后续写·社区温情·转折）

idioms.translation: (关系、计划)遭遇严重挫折,濒临破裂
idioms.example: Their partnership hit the rocks when neither side was willing to admit a single mistake — pride, not distance, had become the real enemy. （议论文·合作与包容·例证）

idioms.idiom: run onto the rocks / go on the rocks
idioms.translation: 触礁;(事业、婚姻)走向失败
idioms.example: Just when the young couple's marriage seemed about to go on the rocks, the arrival of their first child reminded them of the promise they had once made. （读后续写·家庭·转折）

collocations.phrase: on the rocks (= having difficulties / likely to fail soon)
collocations.translation: 【课件】（关系）陷于困境，濒临崩溃（＝in trouble）
collocations.example: Their marriage is on the rocks. 他们的婚姻濒临破裂。(= Their marriage is in trouble.) （课件原句·on the rocks 濒临崩溃）

collocations.translation: 友谊陷入困境（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Friendship on the rocks: please advise! （课文原句·求助帖标题）

collocations.phrase: a relationship / marriage on the rocks
collocations.example: To an outsider they looked like the perfect couple, but their marriage had long been on the rocks. （读后续写·人物反差）
A friendship on the rocks is not necessarily a friendship over. （议论文·友谊·辩证观点）

collocations.phrase: put / drive sth on the rocks
collocations.example: Constant jealousy had slowly driven their once-warm bond on the rocks. （读后续写·情感恶化）

collocations.phrase: whisky / a drink on the rocks
collocations.example: "A whisky on the rocks, please," he said, loosening his tie. （读后续写·人物细节）
With patience on both sides, a relationship can be brought back from the rocks. （议论文·修复关系）
With his family business on the rocks, the young man asked his rival for help. （读后续写·励志转折）

synonyms.example: The moment I saw her red eyes, I knew our friendship was in trouble, and that pretending otherwise would only make things worse. （读后续写·察觉危机）
synonyms.usage: in trouble 为最通用的口语表达,泛指各种困境;on the rocks 更形象生动,专指关系、婚姻、事业濒临破裂

synonyms.example: As misunderstandings piled up like autumn leaves, our friendship was quietly falling apart, and neither of us dared to speak first. （读后续写·关系瓦解·比喻）
synonyms.usage: falling apart 强调'逐渐瓦解'的动态过程,可用于关系、计划、人的精神状态;on the rocks 强调已到'触礁'的危险临界点

synonyms.example: Communication between the two teams had completely broken down, and the project ground to a halt. （议论文·团队协作·因果论证）
synonyms.usage: break down 侧重系统、机制、沟通的'崩溃失灵';on the rocks 是形象习语,专用于关系、婚姻、生意等即将失败的语境

advancedExpressions.expression: on the rocks / hit the rocks / go on the rocks / be back from the rocks
advancedExpressions.example: What had once been the closest friendship was now on the rocks, until one honest apology brought it back from the rocks. （关系由裂到修的短语链）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·陷入困境（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: on the rocks ≈ in trouble ≈ falling apart ≈ breaking down ≈ going downhill
advancedExpressions.example: Our friendship was on the rocks / in trouble / falling apart — no matter how I put it, we were drifting away from each other. （同义替换练关系恶化表达）

advancedExpressions.expression: what had once been ... was now on the rocks, until ...
advancedExpressions.example: What had once been the warmest friendship in our class was now on the rocks, until a single note slipped into my desk — "I miss you" — melted three months of stubborn silence. （今昔对比+悬念细节）

advancedExpressions.expression: my ... seems to be on the rocks, and I would be grateful for any advice on how to ...
advancedExpressions.example: My friendship with my deskmate seems to be on the rocks, and I would be truly grateful for any advice on how to rebuild the trust we have lost. （求助信·委婉陈述困境+明确诉求）

advancedExpressions.expression: a relationship on the rocks can still be steered back to safe waters if ...
advancedExpressions.example: A relationship on the rocks can still be steered back to safe waters if both sides are willing to let understanding, rather than pride, hold the wheel. （航海隐喻贯穿+对比升华）

sentenceUpgrade.original: My friendship with her was in trouble.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The friendship I had treasured for years was suddenly on the rocks, and every unanswered message felt like another wave hammering against a boat I no longer knew how to steer. （读后续写·航海隐喻+心理描写）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: on the rocks 习语替换 in trouble + wave hammering 延续航海意象 + a boat I no longer knew how to steer 外化无助感

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not give up when a relationship has problems.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: When a relationship drifts on the rocks, the wise choice is not to abandon ship but to reach for the oar of honest communication and row, patiently, back towards each other. （议论文·比喻论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: drift on the rocks/abandon ship/oar/row 航海隐喻链 + not to...but to 对比句式 + patiently 副词点睛

classPractice.type: 同义句转换（课件·on the rocks=in trouble）
classPractice.question: Their marriage is in trouble. →用 on the rocks 改写：Their marriage is ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 课件原句；on the rocks ＝ in trouble，专指关系/婚姻/生意濒临破裂，作表语，注意介词 on

classPractice.question:
他们曾经亲密无间的友谊如今濒临破裂。（on the rocks）
Their once-inseparable friendship is now ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: on the rocks 作表语，形容关系/婚姻/生意濒临破裂，注意介词 on

classPractice.question:
用 on the rocks / in trouble 填空（形象习语专用于关系破裂）：
A glass of whisky ____ ____ ____ sat before him, ice slowly melting.
classPractice.note: 此处指饮料"加冰"，只能用 on the rocks；in trouble 无此义

classPractice.question: 当一段关系濒临破裂时，逃避从来都不是答案。
classPractice.answer: When a relationship is on the rocks, running away is never the answer.
classPractice.note: on the rocks 作表语；running away 动名词作主语

translation: 局促不安的；令人尴尬的；难对付的；笨拙的
original_sentence: When I was an awkward primary school student, she was the popular girl who was willing to make friends with me.
readingExamples: When I was an awkward primary school student, she was the popular girl who was willing to make friends with me.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. making you feel embarrassed, uncomfortable or self-conscious in a social situation
(2) adj. difficult to deal with or handle; causing problems and requiring skill or care
(3) adj. not moving in a smooth or graceful way; clumsy in movement or manner
(4) adj. (of a person) deliberately unhelpful or difficult to please

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】笨拙的，不灵活的（not moving in an easy way；clumsy and awkward）
uncommonMeanings.example: He tried to dance, but he was too clumsy and awkward. 他试着跳舞，但太笨拙、太别扭。（课件原句·awkward 笨拙）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】难处理的，难对付的，不好回答的（difficult；an awkward question）
uncommonMeanings.example: The awkward question put the president in a very awkward position. 这个难对付的问题让总统陷入十分尴尬的境地。（课件原句·awkward 难对付）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 笨拙的，不灵活的(形容动作、姿态)
uncommonMeanings.example: With awkward, trembling fingers he tried to tie the bandage, but the harder he tried, the more it slipped. （读后续写·动作细节）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (人)难对付的，不好相处的，故意刁难的
uncommonMeanings.example: The new manager had a reputation for being awkward, refusing every reasonable request just to show his power. （读后续写·人物刻画）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (处境、问题)棘手的,难对付的(而非'尴尬')
uncommonMeanings.example: The teacher's simple question put me in an awkward position: telling the truth would betray a friend, yet a lie would betray myself. （读后续写·道德两难）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (时间、位置)不方便的,别扭的
uncommonMeanings.example: The meeting was scheduled at an awkward hour, right in the middle of the afternoon nap that Grandpa never gave up. （读后续写·生活细节·幽默）

posExamples.sentence: As an awkward new student who knew no one, I hovered at the edge of the noisy playground, until a girl with a bright smile walked over and simply said, "Come sit with us." （读后续写·校园破冰·环境与心理）
If you feel awkward speaking English in front of the whole class, our English corner offers a relaxed and friendly place where making mistakes is not only allowed but welcomed. （应用文·社团招募）
Feeling awkward in an unfamiliar setting is not a weakness but a natural stage of growth; the moment we dare to speak first, awkwardness quietly turns into confidence. （议论文·成长与勇气·观点论证）
An awkward silence fell over the dinner table after my careless remark, and I watched Mum's smile fade like sunlight behind a passing cloud. （读后续写·家庭冲突·比喻）

wordForms.other: 构词法：awkward + -ly → awkwardly（副词）；awkward + -ness → awkwardness（名词）。贴士：awkward 兼"尴尬/笨拙/棘手/难对付"多义，判断词义要看搭配——修饰 silence/moment/position 多为"尴尬"，修饰 fingers/movement 多为"笨拙"，修饰 question/problem 多为"棘手"，形容 person 可为"难相处"。

idioms.example: After his joke fell flat, an awkward silence hung in the room until the shy new boy suddenly laughed, and the ice was broken at last. （读后续写·社交破冰）
His unexpected question put me in an awkward position, torn between loyalty to my friend and honesty to my teacher. （读后续写·道德抉择）

idioms.translation: 青春期尴尬的年纪;青涩年华
idioms.example: At the awkward age of thirteen, everything about myself seemed wrong — too tall, too quiet, too easily embarrassed. （读后续写·青春成长·自我怀疑）

collocations.translation: 【课件】笨拙的，别扭的（not moving in an easy way）
collocations.example: He tried to dance, but he was too clumsy and awkward. 他试着跳舞，但是太笨拙、太别扭。（课件原句·awkward 笨拙）
At the press conference, there was a long awkward silence. 记者招待会上出现了长时间令人尴尬的沉默。（课件原句·awkward 尴尬）
The awkward question put the president in a very awkward position. 这个难对付的问题让总统陷入十分尴尬的境地。（课件原句·awkward 难对付＋尴尬）

collocations.phrase: put sb in an awkward position (令人尴尬的处境)
collocations.translation: 【课件】使某人陷入尴尬的境地（embarrassing）
collocations.example: The awkward question put the president in a very awkward position. 这个难题使总统处境十分尴尬。（课件原句·awkward position）

collocations.phrase: feel awkward (and uncomfortable) 感到局促
collocations.translation: 【课件】感到局促不安的，感到别扭（embarrassed）
collocations.example: He felt awkward and uncomfortable. 他感到局促不安、浑身不自在。（课件原句·feel awkward 感到局促）

collocations.translation: 一个局促不安的小学生（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: When I was an awkward primary school student, she was the popular girl who was willing to make friends with me. （课文原句·Amy's post）
I felt so awkward standing alone at the party that I pretended to be absorbed in my phone. （读后续写·社交焦虑）
An awkward silence fell over the table after my careless remark. （读后续写·家庭冲突）
Learning to handle awkward situations with grace is a valuable skill. （议论文·情商与成长）
There was an awkward moment when I called my new teacher by the wrong name. （读后续写·校园幽默）
The reporter's awkward question left the young champion silent for a long moment. （读后续写·人物刻画）
At first I felt awkward about asking for help, but I soon learned it is a kind of strength. （议论文·成长感悟）
She was passing through that awkward age when a single unkind comment could ruin a week. （读后续写·青春敏感）
Rather than making things awkward by refusing outright, she gently explained her reasons. （应用文·委婉表达）

synonyms.example: Cheeks burning, the embarrassed boy stared at his shoes as the whole class turned to look at him. （读后续写·羞窘·动作描写）
synonyms.usage: embarrassed 直接描述人内心'难为情'的情绪;awkward 既可形容人不自在,也可形容气氛、处境、动作,范围更广

synonyms.example: With clumsy fingers he tried to tie the ribbon, but the harder he tried, the more hopelessly it tangled. （读后续写·动作细节）
synonyms.usage: clumsy 专指动作笨拙、不协调;awkward 表'笨拙'时含义相近,但更常用于形容社交尴尬和棘手处境

synonyms.example: She shifted uncomfortably in her seat as the questions grew more and more personal. （读后续写·心理不适）
synonyms.usage: uncomfortable 泛指身体或心理上的'不舒服';awkward 特指因社交场合或处境而产生的'别扭、尴尬'

synonyms.example: Balancing honesty and kindness in a reply is a tricky task that even adults sometimes get wrong. （议论文·人际智慧）
synonyms.usage: tricky 侧重问题'复杂难解、需要技巧';awkward 表'棘手'时更强调因两难或不便而'令人为难'

advancedExpressions.expression: feel awkward / an awkward silence / in an awkward position / make things awkward
advancedExpressions.example: Feeling awkward, I broke the awkward silence before it put us both in an awkward position. （尴尬语境短语串联）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·尴尬不自在（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: feel awkward ≈ feel embarrassed ≈ feel uncomfortable ≈ feel ill at ease ≈ feel out of place
advancedExpressions.example: Standing among strangers, I felt awkward / embarrassed / out of place, longing to disappear. （同义替换练"不自在"）

advancedExpressions.expression: awkward(adj.) → awkwardly(adv.) → awkwardness(n.)
advancedExpressions.example: He smiled awkwardly, and the awkwardness between us grew heavier by the second. （一句串起形容词/副词/名词三形）

advancedExpressions.expression: the awkward silence was broken when ...
advancedExpressions.example: The awkward silence was broken when the shyest boy in the room suddenly held out half of his sandwich — a small gesture that turned a stranger into a friend. （细节动作打破僵局）

advancedExpressions.expression: if you feel awkward about ..., remember that ...
advancedExpressions.example: If you feel awkward about speaking up in class, remember that everyone around you shares the same fear. （建议信·共情+鼓励）

advancedExpressions.expression: far from being a flaw, awkwardness is ...
advancedExpressions.example: Far from being a flaw to be ashamed of, awkwardness is simply the growing pain of a person daring to step beyond the familiar. （far from 否定+隐喻重新定义）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I felt awkward when I met new people.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Whenever I faced a room of unfamiliar faces, an awkward heat would creep up my neck, my carefully rehearsed greetings dissolving into a clumsy, half-swallowed "hi". （读后续写·社交焦虑·生理细节）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: an awkward heat crept up my neck 生理反应外化情绪 + carefully rehearsed...dissolving 反差 + half-swallowed 精准修饰

sentenceUpgrade.original: It is normal for teenagers to feel awkward.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: It should be recognized that the awkwardness so common among teenagers is not a defect to be corrected but a bridge every one of us must cross on the way to a more confident self. （议论文·辩证论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: It should be recognized that 正式句式 + not...but 对比重新定义 + a bridge...must cross 隐喻升华

classPractice.type: 辨析选词（课件·awkward 一词多义）
classPractice.question: 用 awkward 填空并说明含义：After his rude remark, there was a long ____ silence (____); the reporter's ____ question (____) then put him in a very ____ position (____).
classPractice.answer: awkward（尴尬的）；awkward（难对付的）；awkward（尴尬的）
classPractice.note: 课件语境：修饰 silence/position 多为"尴尬"(embarrassing)，修饰 question 多为"难对付"(difficult)，一词多义靠搭配判断

classPractice.type: 完成句子（课件·feel awkward 感到局促）
classPractice.question: 他感到局促不安、浑身不自在。He ____ ____ and uncomfortable.
classPractice.note: 课件原句 He felt awkward and uncomfortable；feel awkward 感到局促、不自在（embarrassed）

classPractice.question: He smiled ____ (awkward) and looked away, not knowing what to say.
classPractice.note: 修饰动词 smiled 用副词 awkwardly；awkward 结尾加 -ly 不去 d

classPractice.question: 从 awkward / embarrassed 中选词：An ____ silence fell over the room after his rude remark.
classPractice.note: 修饰 silence（气氛/处境）用 awkward；embarrassed 只形容"人内心难为情"，不修饰 silence

classPractice.question:
老师的问题让我陷入尴尬的境地。（position）
The teacher's question put me ____ ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 固定搭配 put sb in an awkward position "使某人处境尴尬/两难"，此处 awkward 意为"棘手、两难"

original_sentence: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
readingExamples: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
definitionEn:
(1) n. the ability to see; the power of vision
(2) n. the act of seeing something, or the fact that it can be seen; the range within which something can be seen
(3) n. a thing that is seen; a view or spectacle, especially a remarkable or memorable one
(4) n. (usually plural, sights) places of interest that people visit as tourists

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】视力，视觉（have good / poor sight = eyesight；near-/short-sighted, far-/long-sighted）
uncommonMeanings.example: have good / poor sight (eyesight); near-sighted / short-sighted 近视的、目光短浅的; far-sighted / long-sighted 远视的、有远见的。（课件·sight 视力归纳）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】(常用 pl. sights)名胜，景点（see the sights；the main/major sights）
uncommonMeanings.example: Our final day saw us tour the main sights of Paris. (= see the sights) 最后一天我们游览了巴黎的主要景点。（课件·sights 名胜 + sightseeing 观光）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 视力，视觉(能力)
uncommonMeanings.example: Years of reading in dim light had gradually weakened his sight, yet he refused to stop turning pages. （读后续写·人物·坚持）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 景象，眼前所见之物；(pl. sights)名胜，风景
uncommonMeanings.example: As we reached the hilltop, the most breathtaking sight unfolded before us — a sea of clouds glowing gold. （读后续写·景物描写）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 看见，瞥见；(尤指经搜寻后)发现
uncommonMeanings.example: After days adrift, the exhausted crew finally sighted land, and a ragged cheer broke across the deck. （读后续写·脱险）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (常用 a sight)一副糟糕/滑稽的样子;(口语)难看的景象
uncommonMeanings.example: Soaked to the skin and covered in mud, I must have been a sight, yet Grandma only laughed. （读后续写·祖孙温情·幽默）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (枪炮的)瞄准器,准星
uncommonMeanings.example: The young hunter lined up the deer in his sights, but the moment their eyes met, his finger froze. （读后续写·抉择时刻）

posExamples.sentence: The train pulled away, and I pressed my face to the window until my hometown finally disappeared from sight, taking a piece of my heart with it. （读后续写·离别·环境与心理）
During the field trip, please stay within sight of your group leader at all times, as the mountain paths can be steep and easy to lose your way on. （应用文·安全须知/通知）
We should never lose sight of the fact that success is measured not only by grades, but by the kindness and courage we show along the way. （议论文·价值观·观点论证）
As we reached the hilltop, the most breathtaking sight unfolded before us — a sea of clouds glowing gold in the first light of dawn. （读后续写·自然风光·景物描写）

wordForms.adjective: sightless (adj. 失明的); sighted (adj. 有视力的)
wordForms.other: sightseeing (n. 观光,游览); sightseer (n. 观光者); insight (n. 洞察力); foresight (n. 远见); eyesight (n. 视力)

idioms.idiom: out of sight, out of mind
idioms.translation: 眼不见,心不烦;久别情疏
idioms.example: People say out of sight, out of mind, yet the friend who moved abroad still writes to me every festival — some bonds simply refuse to fade. （议论文·友谊·反驳论证）
At first sight the old house seemed cold and unwelcoming, but the moment I stepped inside, the smell of fresh bread told a warmer story. （读后续写·反差·细节描写）
For Grandpa it was love at first sight — sixty years on, he still describes the exact dress Grandma wore that spring afternoon. （读后续写·家史温情）

idioms.translation: 看不见;忽视,忘记(重要的事)
idioms.example: In the endless race for higher marks, we must never lose sight of why we began to learn in the first place. （议论文·教育初心）
Just as I was giving up hope, I caught sight of a familiar red umbrella pushing through the crowd — Mum had come for me after all. （读后续写·寻找·转折）

idioms.translation: 令人眼前一亮的人/物;久违的喜人景象
idioms.example: After a week lost in the mountains, the distant lights of the village were a sight for sore eyes. （读后续写·脱险·情感释放）

collocations.translation: 【课件】看得见（在视线范围内）／看不见（在视线之外）
collocations.example: There was no one in sight. 一个人也看不见。（课件原句·in sight 在视线范围内）
At first sight, it may look like a generous offer. 乍一看，这似乎是一个慷慨的提议。（课件原句·at first sight）
I have been known to faint at the sight of blood. 众所周知我一看到血就会晕倒。（课件原句·at the sight of）
She caught sight of a car in the distance. 她瞥见远处有一辆汽车。（课件原句·catch sight of）
We must not lose sight of our original aim. 我们绝不能忘记（忽视）我们最初的目标。（课件原句·lose sight of）
A bicycle came into sight on the main road. 一辆自行车出现在主路上。（课件原句·come into sight）

collocations.phrase: see the sights / the main (major) sights
collocations.translation: 【课件】观光，游览（主要）名胜景点
collocations.example: Our final day, Friday, saw us visit central Paris and tour the main sights. 最后一天星期五，我们游览巴黎市中心，参观主要景点。(= see the sights) （课件原句·see the sights）
We treated our foreign guests to a day's sightseeing around the ancient city. 我们带外国客人在古城观光了一天。（课件·sightseeing 观光）
Years of reading in the dark left him with poor sight, yet he never once complained. 多年在昏暗中读书使他视力变差，可他从未抱怨。（课件·sight 视力 have good/poor sight）

collocations.translation: 【课件】近视的；目光短浅的／远视的；有远见的
collocations.example: A short-sighted plan may bring quick profit, but only a far-sighted vision builds a lasting future. 目光短浅的计划或许带来快钱，唯有远见卓识才能筑就长久的未来。（课件·sight 归纳 near-/short-/far-/long-sighted）

collocations.translation: 在彼此的视线之外（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight. （课文原句·Amy's post）
With the finish line finally in sight, the exhausted runner surged forward. （读后续写·体育励志）
She waved until the bus turned the corner and her mother was out of sight. （读后续写·离别）
As the fog lifted, a small fishing village came into sight. （读后续写·景物描写）
Just as I was giving up hope, I caught sight of a familiar red umbrella in the crowd. （读后续写·转折）
Amid all the busy revision, we should not lose sight of the importance of rest. （议论文·平衡）
At the sight of her old diary, a flood of forgotten summers came rushing back. （读后续写·回忆）
At first sight the problem looked impossible, but breaking it into steps revealed a clear way through. （议论文·方法）
Our foreign friends are eager to see the sights of our ancient city. （应用文·行程安排）
The cottage stood in sight of the sea, and every morning we woke to the sound of waves. （读后续写·环境描写）
I knew the quiet librarian only by sight, until the day she saved the very book I had dreamed of reading. （读后续写·温情）

synonyms.translation: 场景,景象;(事件发生的)现场
synonyms.example: The scene at the railway station moved everyone to tears: soldiers embracing their families. （读后续写·情感场景）
synonyms.usage: scene 指含人物活动或情节的"场面、情景"，常与事件相关，可数（a moving scene）；sight 更强调纯视觉上"看到的东西"，往往令人印象深刻（a beautiful sight）。位置上二者都可作宾语，但"at the sight of"是固定搭配，不能换成 scene

synonyms.translation: (某地区的)自然风光，景色(总称)
synonyms.example: We drove for hours through the mountains, drinking in the magnificent scenery on every side. （读后续写·旅途）
synonyms.usage: scenery 是不可数名词，泛指一个地区"整体的自然风光"，前不加 a、不用复数；sight 可数，指某个具体景象或（复数 sights）名胜。说"美景"用 beautiful scenery，说"一处景点"用 a sight

synonyms.example: From the top floor, the view of the city lights stretched endlessly. （读后续写·景物+心理）
synonyms.usage: view 侧重"从某一位置望出去所见的景色"，强调视角，常搭配 a view of sth / from...；sight 侧重某个具体、往往令人印象深刻的"景象"本身，不强调观看位置

synonyms.example: Years of reading in dim light had weakened his vision, yet his imagination remained sharp. （读后续写·人物·反差）
synonyms.usage: vision 较正式，既指"视力"，也常引申为"远见、愿景"（a leader of vision）；sight 更日常，侧重"看见的能力"与"看到的景象"，无"愿景"之义

synonyms.example: The dragon-boat race was a spectacle of colour and thunderous drums. （应用文·活动介绍）
synonyms.usage: spectacle 特指"盛大、壮观"的场面，感情色彩强，多含惊叹；sight 中性，普通景象与壮丽景象皆可用

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·whether...or 引导让步状语从句（课件·Reading）
advancedExpressions.expression: 【课件】Whether ... or ..., ... 不管……还是……，引导让步状语从句（sight 出现于课文原句 out of each other's sight）
advancedExpressions.example: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight. 无论是一起走路上学、写作业，还是周末只是随便逛逛，我们几乎都不离开彼此的视线。（课文原句 + 课件语法讲解：Whether…or… 引导让步状从）

advancedExpressions.type: 短语群·视线的出现与消失
advancedExpressions.expression: come into sight / catch sight of / lose sight of / out of sight / at first sight
advancedExpressions.example: The moment the village came into sight I caught sight of Mum's figure, and I never once lost sight of her until the road curved and she slipped out of sight. （视线短语连缀成情节）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·消失不见（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: disappear from sight ≈ vanish from sight ≈ fade from sight ≈ be lost to view
advancedExpressions.example: The little green train slowly disappeared / vanished / faded from sight, and the platform fell silent. （同义替换练"消失"）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·at the sight of vs at first sight
advancedExpressions.expression: at the sight of + n.（一看见……就）/ at first sight（乍一看；初次见面）
advancedExpressions.example: At first sight he seemed cold, but at the sight of a lost child crying he rushed over at once. （两个 sight 固定短语对比，词义与用法不同）

advancedExpressions.expression: ... until ... finally faded / disappeared from sight
advancedExpressions.example: I stood rooted to the platform, waving and waving, until the little green train finally faded from sight and the silence felt almost unbearable. （动作重复+视觉消退）

advancedExpressions.expression: we must not lose sight of ...
advancedExpressions.example: While chasing higher scores, we must not lose sight of the true purpose of education — to grow into thoughtful, caring individuals. （建议信·提醒初心）

advancedExpressions.expression: the true goal ... should never slip out of sight
advancedExpressions.example: In an age dazzled by instant success, the true goal of learning — cultivating wisdom rather than merely storing facts — should never slip out of sight. （视觉隐喻+破折号补充）

sentenceUpgrade.original: I watched him leave until I could not see him.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: I watched his figure grow smaller and smaller until it melted into the crowd and vanished from sight, and only then did I realize how much I would miss him. （读后续写·离别·倒装心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: grow smaller and smaller 渐进 + melted into/vanished from sight 视觉消退 + only then did I realize 倒装点出情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: We should not forget our original goal.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: However fierce the competition may become, we must never lose sight of the goal that first set us on this journey, for a traveller who forgets the destination will only wander in circles. （议论文·比喻论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: However...may become 让步状语从句 + lose sight of 习语 + a traveller who...隐喻说理

classPractice.type: 用 sight 短语填空（课件·视线短语群）
classPractice.question:
用 sight 的固定短语填空：
(1) There was no one ____ ____ (看得见).
(2) She ____ ____ ____ a car in the distance (瞥见).
(3) We must not ____ ____ ____ our original aim (忘记，忽视).
(4) A bicycle ____ ____ ____ on the main road (进入视线).
classPractice.answer: (1) in sight (2) caught sight of (3) lose sight of (4) came into sight
classPractice.note: 课件原句改编：in sight 看得见；catch sight of 瞥见；lose sight of 忽视/忘记；come into sight 出现

classPractice.type: 完成句子（课件·see the sights）
classPractice.question: 最后一天我们游览巴黎市中心，参观主要景点。On our final day, we visited central Paris and toured ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 课件原句；see/tour the sights ＝ 观光；(pl.) sights 名胜、景点

classPractice.question:
用 sight 的固定短语填空：
As the fog lifted, a small lighthouse gradually came ____ ____.（进入视野）
classPractice.note: come into sight "进入视野、出现"；注意介词 into

classPractice.question:
从 sight / scenery / view 中选词：
We stopped the car simply to enjoy the beautiful mountain ____ (自然风光·不可数).
classPractice.note: 泛指一片地区的自然风光用不可数名词 scenery，不加 a、不用复数；sight/view 均可数，词义侧重不同

classPractice.question:
我们绝不能忽视健康的重要性。（lose）
We should never ____ ____ ____ the importance of health.
classPractice.note: lose sight of sth "忽视、忘记（重要之事）"，此处 sight 为引申义"注意、着眼"

original_sentence: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
readingExamples: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
definitionEn:
(1) phr. beyond the range of someone's vision; in a place where a particular person cannot see it
(2) phr. away from someone's watchful attention or supervision

posExamples.sentence: The mother did not relax for a single second until the school bus turned the corner and her little son was out of her sight, and even then she stood waving at the empty street. （读后续写·母爱·细节描写）
For safety reasons, young children should never be left out of an adult's sight while playing near the water during the summer camp. （应用文·安全须知）
Real trust means allowing those we love to step out of our sight, confident that the values we have shared will guide them wherever they go. （议论文·信任与放手·观点论证）
The moment the guard was out of my sight, I slipped through the half-open gate, my heart pounding so loudly I feared the whole world could hear it. （读后续写·冒险·心理紧张）

idioms.idiom: out of sight, out of mind
idioms.translation: 眼不见,心不烦;久别情疏
idioms.example: They warned me that friends who move away soon fade — out of sight, out of mind — but a single handwritten letter each month proved them wonderfully wrong. （议论文·友谊·反驳论证）

idioms.translation: 躲开某人的视线,避免被某人看见
idioms.example: The stray puppy learned to keep out of the shopkeeper's sight, waiting in the shadows until a kind hand finally reached out to it. （读后续写·流浪动物·温情）

collocations.phrase: out of one's sight (表状态) 看不见
collocations.translation: 【课件】看不见，脱离某人视线（表状态）
collocations.example: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight. 无论走路上学、写作业，还是周末闲逛，我们几乎都不离开彼此的视线。（课件原句·out of one's sight 看不见）

collocations.translation: 在彼此的视线之外（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight. （课文原句·Amy's post）

collocations.phrase: be hardly out of sb's sight
collocations.translation: 几乎不离开某人的视线;形影不离
collocations.example: Throughout that summer, the two best friends were hardly out of each other's sight. （读后续写·友谊）
I chased the balloon until it drifted over the rooftops and vanished out of sight. （读后续写·童年·怅惘）

collocations.phrase: keep sb / sth out of sight
collocations.translation: 把某人/某物藏起来不让看见
collocations.example: She quickly slid the surprise gift out of sight the moment she heard footsteps. （读后续写·惊喜）
"Get out of my sight!" he shouted — words he would spend the night wishing he could take back. （读后续写·冲突·悔恨）
The frightened kitten stayed out of sight beneath the sofa until a gentle voice coaxed it out. （读后续写·救助动物）
Behind his cheerful smile, hidden out of sight, lay a loneliness only his diary knew. （读后续写·人物内心）

synonyms.example: The little boat slipped quietly out of view behind the misty headland, and the harbour fell strangely still. （读后续写·景物·氛围）
synonyms.usage: out of view 侧重客观'不在视野范围内';out of one's sight 更强调'某个特定的人'看不见,常带情感色彩

synonyms.translation: 在某人够不到/控制不到的地方
synonyms.example: Once her children grew up and moved beyond her reach, the old mother learned the hardest lesson of love: to trust and to let go. （议论文·放手·亲情）
synonyms.usage: beyond one's reach 侧重'触及不到、掌控不了';out of one's sight 侧重'看不见',二者常在'放手'语境中互补

synonyms.translation: 未被看见的,不为人知的
synonyms.example: Countless unseen acts of kindness quietly hold our society together, though they rarely make the headlines. （议论文·善行·观点句）
synonyms.usage: unseen 为形容词,修饰'未被注意到'的事物;out of one's sight 为短语,强调暂时脱离某人的视线

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·whether...or 引导让步状语从句（课件·Reading）
advancedExpressions.expression: 【课件】Whether ... or ..., ... 不管……还是……，引导让步状语从句（课文正是 Whether we're...or..., we're hardly out of each other's sight）
advancedExpressions.example: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight. 无论是走路上学、写作业，还是周末闲逛，我们几乎都不离开彼此的视线。／ All people, whether they are old or young, rich or poor, have been making every effort to help those in need since the disaster. （课件原句 + 拓展例句：Whether…or… 引导让步状从，从句可省略主语和 be 动词）

advancedExpressions.expression: out of one's sight / stay out of sight / keep sth out of sight / vanish out of sight
advancedExpressions.example: She kept the letter out of sight and stayed out of sight herself until the visitor had vanished out of sight down the lane. （脱离视线短语串）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·脱离某人视线（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: out of one's sight ≈ out of view ≈ beyond one's sight ≈ where sb cannot see
advancedExpressions.example: The boat slipped out of my sight / out of view / beyond my sight behind the misty headland. （同义替换练"看不见了"）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·out of sight, out of mind
advancedExpressions.expression: Out of sight, out of mind.（谚语：眼不见，心不烦；久别情疏）
advancedExpressions.example: People say out of sight, out of mind, yet the friend who moved abroad still writes every festival. （谚语引用+反驳，续写/议论皆宜）

advancedExpressions.expression: sb. did not move / stop ... until ... was out of sight
advancedExpressions.example: Mum did not turn back to the house until the last flicker of my figure was out of sight, and she stood there long after the road lay empty. （延迟动作+补叙，双向牵挂）

advancedExpressions.expression: please make sure ... is never out of your sight
advancedExpressions.example: During the outing, please make sure your younger partner is never out of your sight, especially near the lake. （安全须知·祈使句+场景）

advancedExpressions.expression: to love someone is to let them step out of our sight and still believe in them
advancedExpressions.example: To love someone truly is to let them step out of our sight and still believe, wholeheartedly, that they will find their own way home. （对"爱"的哲理定义+升华）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She watched her son until she could not see him.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: She stood at the gate, her eyes following her son's every step until his small backpack bobbed round the corner and slipped out of her sight, and only then did she let the tears fall. （读后续写·母爱·倒装心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: her eyes following...every step 视线追踪 + backpack bobbed 生动动词 + slipped out of her sight + only then did she 倒装点情感

sentenceUpgrade.original: Parents should let their children be independent.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Genuine love does not cling; it dares to let a child walk out of our sight, trusting that the roots of care we have planted will hold firm against any storm ahead. （议论文·比喻论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: does not cling 拟人否定 + walk out of our sight 具象化'放手' + roots...hold firm against any storm 隐喻说理

classPractice.type: 翻译句子（课件·whether...or + out of one's sight 原句）
classPractice.question: 无论是走路上学、写作业，还是周末闲逛，我们几乎都不离开彼此的视线。（Whether...or; out of one's sight）
classPractice.answer: Whether we're walking to school, doing homework or just hanging out at the weekend, we're hardly out of each other's sight.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；Whether…or… 引导让步状从，out of one's sight 表"看不见"的状态，注意 each other's

classPractice.question:
母亲一直站在门口，直到儿子的身影消失在她的视线之外。（out of, sight）
The mother kept standing at the gate until her son ____ ____ ____ her sight.
classPractice.answer: was out of / went out of / slipped out of
classPractice.note: out of one's sight "在某人视线之外"，可搭配 be / go / slip 等；注意物主代词 her

classPractice.question: 俗话说眼不见，心不烦，但真正的友谊不会因距离而褪色。
classPractice.answer: As the saying goes, out of sight, out of mind, but true friendship never fades because of distance.
classPractice.note: 谚语 out of sight, out of mind 直接引用；用作让步铺垫

classPractice.question:
露营时请确保年幼的同伴始终不脱离你的视线。
Please make sure your young partner is never ____ ____ your sight during the camp.
classPractice.note: out of one's sight 表"脱离某人视线"；never ... out of 表"始终不离开"

original_sentence: Our original plan was to see a film at the cinema that afternoon.
readingExamples: Our original plan was to see a film at the cinema that afternoon.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. existing from the beginning; first or earliest; done or made before anything else of the same kind
(2) adj. new and interesting in a way that is different from anything before; showing fresh thought and creativity
(3) adj. (of a work of art, document, etc.) genuine and not a copy or reproduction
(4) n. the first form of something, from which copies are later made

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 独创的，新颖的，非模仿的
uncommonMeanings.example: The judges praised her design as truly original, admiring how she had turned a common problem into an uncommon solution. （应用文·比赛报道）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 原作的，真迹的(非复制品)
uncommonMeanings.example: Experts confirmed that the dusty canvas in the attic was an original Van Gogh, and the whole town held its breath. （读后续写·意外发现）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 原件,原作(相对于复制品)
uncommonMeanings.example: Everyone assumed the painting was a cheap print, until an expert whispered that it was, unbelievably, the original. （读后续写·悬念）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (常带幽默)有个性的人,与众不同的怪才
uncommonMeanings.example: Our art teacher was a true original, arriving each morning on a rusty bicycle and greeting the sunrise like an old friend. （读后续写·人物刻画·幽默）

posExamples.sentence: Our original plan had been to picnic by the river, but the sudden downpour turned the afternoon into something far more memorable — a wet, laughing dash for the nearest shelter. （读后续写·计划生变·叙事转折）
We warmly encourage every participant to submit an original story that has never been published elsewhere, so that this year's magazine may truly reflect the creativity of our students. （应用文·征稿启事）
In an age when ideas can be copied in a click, original thinking has become the most valuable ability a young person can cultivate. （议论文·创新·观点论证）
Restoring the ancient temple to its original glory took the craftsmen three long years, yet the moment the doors reopened, the whole town fell silent in awe. （读后续写·文化传承·细节描写）

wordForms.noun: origin (n. 起源,出身); originality (n. 独创性,新颖)
wordForms.other: 构词法：origin(n.根/起源) → original(adj.最初的/原创的) → originally(adv.起初) → originality(n.独创性) → originate(v.起源) → originator(n.创始人)。同一词根 origin(起源)。贴士：original 有"最初的/原创的/原件的"三义——修饰 plan/idea/purpose 多为"最初的"，修饰 thinking/design 多为"原创的"，the original 作名词指"原件、原作"。

collocations.translation: 【课件】原定于，原先安排的（originally 为副词，起初、原来）
collocations.example: She got me back to the UK earlier than originally scheduled. 她让我比原定时间更早回到了英国。 （课件Reading·slide8·adv.起初/原来）

collocations.phrase: turn one's original ideas into reality
collocations.translation: 【课件】把独创的想法变为现实（original adj.独创的、新颖的）
collocations.example: The world moves on because of those who are ready to turn their original ideas into reality. 世界向前发展，是因为有那些愿意把自己独创的想法变为现实的人。 （课件Reading·slide8·adj.独创的·填空原题）

collocations.translation: 【课件】最初的计划/想法（original adj.原先的、最初的）
collocations.example: Our original plan was to see a film at the cinema that afternoon. 我们最初的计划是那天下午去电影院看电影。 （课件Reading·slide8·adj.原先的·课文原句）

collocations.translation: 我们最初的计划是……（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Our original plan was to see a film at the cinema that afternoon. （课文原句·Amy's post）
Although our original idea failed, the mistakes led us to a solution none of us had imagined. （读后续写·失败与转机）

collocations.translation: 原主人/原作者/原始版本

synonyms.example: The creative solution she proposed left even the strictest teacher nodding in quiet admiration. （读后续写·人物才华）

synonyms.example: My initial fear of public speaking gradually gave way to a strange, thrilling excitement. （读后续写·心理转变）

synonyms.example: The teacher introduced a novel way of learning grammar through games, and dull rules suddenly came alive. （应用文·活动介绍）

advancedExpressions.expression: our original plan ... , yet what happened next ...

translation: 传播信息的媒介，方法；手段，工具 | adj. 中等的，中号的
original_sentence: But in the morning, my friend posted a message on social media saying she had a cold.
readingExamples: But in the morning, my friend posted a message on social media saying she had a cold.
definitionEn:
(1) n. a means or method by which something is expressed, communicated or achieved; a channel of communication
(2) n. a substance or material used by an artist, or a form of art such as painting, film or music
(3) n. a substance or environment in which something exists, grows or is transmitted
(4) adj. middle in size, amount, degree or position; neither large nor small, high nor low

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 中等的，适中的(大小、程度、身高等居中)
uncommonMeanings.example: She was of medium height, with an ordinary face, yet her quiet kindness made her unforgettable. （读后续写·人物刻画）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (艺术的)表现形式、材料(如绘画、雕塑、电影)
uncommonMeanings.example: For a boy who found it hard to speak, the pencil became his truest medium, telling the world what his voice could not. （读后续写·艺术疗愈）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 灵媒,通灵者(声称能与死者沟通的人)
uncommonMeanings.example: Desperate for one last word with her late husband, the old woman visited a so-called medium. （读后续写·情感·反思）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (生物、化学中的)培养基,介质
uncommonMeanings.example: The scientist carefully placed the sample in a nutrient medium and waited for the first faint sign of life. （读后续写·科研·坚持）

posExamples.sentence: For a lonely boy who found it hard to speak, the pencil became his truest medium, and through countless sketches he finally told the world everything his voice could not. （读后续写·艺术疗愈·人物成长）
Social media has become the most powerful medium for spreading ideas among young people, so we sincerely invite you to share our reading campaign on your accounts. （应用文·倡议书）
The internet, as a double-edged medium, can either broaden our horizons or narrow our minds, depending entirely on how wisely we choose to use it. （议论文·媒介·辩证论证）
She was of medium height, with an ordinary face you might pass a hundred times, yet her quiet kindness made her utterly unforgettable to everyone who knew her. （读后续写·人物刻画·反差）

wordForms.other: 特例·复数：media（用于"媒体/传播媒介"，如 the media, social media）；mediums（用于"灵媒"或"中号商品"等）。相关词：mass media(大众传媒); multimedia(n./adj. 多媒体的); medium-sized(adj. 中等大小的)。贴士：medium 既是名词"媒介/中间物"，也是形容词"中等的"，判断看搭配：a medium of/for → 名词"媒介"；of medium height/size → 形容词"中等"。

idioms.translation: 媒介即讯息(传播学名言:传播方式本身就在传递意义)
idioms.example: As the famous saying goes, the medium is the message, reminding us that how we communicate often matters as much as what we say. （议论文·媒介与沟通·引言论证）

idioms.translation: 找到折中的办法,取得平衡(过与不及之间的中间点)
idioms.example: Between working herself to exhaustion and giving up altogether, she finally struck a happy medium, learning that steady effort beats desperate bursts. （读后续写·自我调节·成长）

collocations.translation: 【课件】中等身高/身材（medium adj.中等的、中号的）
collocations.example: He is of medium height/build, neither too thin nor too fat. 他中等身材，不胖也不瘦。 （课件Reading·slide9·adj.中等的）
They settled in a medium-sized town far from the noisy city. 他们在一个远离喧嚣都市的中等城镇安顿下来。 （课件Reading·slide9·medium-sized 中等大小的）
In the medium term, the project is expected to bring real change to the village. 从中期来看，这个项目有望给村庄带来真正的改变。 （课件Reading·slide9·medium 中等的）
Long before the telephone, letters were the warmest medium of communication. （读后续写·书信·温情）
Through the medium of music, students who shared no common language found they could understand one another. （应用文·文化交流）
Volunteering became a wonderful medium for shy students to build confidence. （应用文·活动总结）
Used wisely, social media connects us; used carelessly, it isolates us behind a glowing screen. （议论文·对比论证）
The mass media shape not only what we know, but often how we feel about what we know. （议论文·媒体影响力）
The stranger was of medium build, unremarkable, until he stepped forward to help the fallen man. （读后续写·人物·反差）
The charity is looking for medium-sized boxes to pack winter clothes for children. （应用文·募捐通知）
In balancing study and rest, most students learn to find a happy medium. （议论文·平衡之道）

synonyms.example: For migrant workers far from home, a video call is often the only means of watching their children grow up. （读后续写·亲情）
synonyms.usage: means 泛指达成目的的"手段、方法"，用途极广，单复数同形（a means of / by means of）；medium 特指"传播、表达的媒介或艺术形式"，更具体，复数为 media

synonyms.example: The suggestion box offers every student a safe channel to voice concerns. （应用文·校园管理）
synonyms.usage: channel 侧重信息、资源"流通的通道、途径"（a channel to/for）；medium 侧重承载和传递信息的"媒介本身"（the medium of TV）

synonyms.example: His grades were merely average, yet his boundless curiosity set him apart. （读后续写·人物·反差）
synonyms.usage: average 侧重"平均水平、一般的"，常带"不突出"意味；medium 作形容词时纯指尺寸、程度"居中"，中性不含评价（medium size / of medium height）

advancedExpressions.expression: a medium of communication / through the medium of / the mass media / find a happy medium
advancedExpressions.example: Through the medium of art, she communicated what words could not, and in her life she always found a happy medium between work and rest. （medium 多义搭配串联）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·传播媒介（可替换，表"媒介"义时）
advancedExpressions.expression: medium ≈ means ≈ channel ≈ vehicle（作"传播/表达媒介"）
advancedExpressions.example: Music can be a powerful medium / means / channel / vehicle for spreading ideas. （表"媒介"时可替换；表"中等"义则不可换）

advancedExpressions.expression: medium(单) → media(复,媒体) / mediums(复,灵媒); mass media; multimedia; medium-sized
advancedExpressions.example: The media (复数) love a story, but each medium (单数) — print, TV, the web — tells it in its own way. （单复数与派生词一句呈现）

advancedExpressions.expression: through the medium of ..., sb. found a voice they never knew they had
advancedExpressions.example: Through the medium of painting, the silent boy found a voice he never knew he had, and colour by colour, a hidden world came pouring onto the page. （以媒介刻画觉醒）

advancedExpressions.expression: as the most influential medium among young people, ... can ...
advancedExpressions.example: As the most influential medium among young people today, social media can turn a single kind idea into a wave of action. （倡议书·点明力量+号召）

advancedExpressions.expression: ... is a neutral medium; whether it blesses or harms us depends on ...
advancedExpressions.example: The internet is in itself a neutral medium; whether it becomes a window to the world or a wall around the mind depends on the hand that holds it. （neutral medium 立论+对比隐喻）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He used drawing to express his feelings.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Unable to put his grief into words, he turned to drawing as his medium, and every trembling line on the paper spoke louder than any sentence ever could. （读后续写·艺术抒情·细节）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Unable to...分词状语前置 + turned to...as his medium 精准用词 + every trembling line spoke louder 拟人对比

sentenceUpgrade.original: Social media has both good and bad effects.

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: neither saint nor villain 拟人对比 + magnifies whatever we bring 因果概括 + rewarding A with B / C with D 平行结构说理

posExamples.sentence: That night she scrolled through social media until the small hours, her thumb trembling as one cruel comment after another lit up the screen — each notification a fresh wound she could not stop pressing. （读后续写·网络暴力·心理描写）
I am writing to propose that our school launch a campaign on social media to raise awareness of the growing problem of food waste in the canteen. （应用文·建议信）
While social media has undeniably brought the world closer, it has, paradoxically, driven many people further apart, replacing genuine conversation with a stream of hollow likes. （议论文·科技与人际关系）
The moment the rescue video was posted on social media, it spread like wildfire, and by dawn a quiet act of kindness had inspired millions across the country. （读后续写·善举传播·情节推进）

collocations.translation: 在社交媒体上迅速走红

collocations.translation: 在社交媒体上散布谣言

collocations.translation: 社交媒体网红/有影响力的人
collocations.example: Overnight she was transformed into a social media influencer, yet fame proved a heavier crown than she had expected. （读后续写·名利反思）

collocations.translation: 社交媒体上的活跃度/影响力
collocations.example: The small bookshop built a loyal following by cultivating a warm, personal social media presence rather than relying on flashy advertisements. （应用文·活动感悟）

synonyms.example: The charity used a popular online platform to connect donors directly with the families they were helping. （应用文·公益活动）
synonyms.usage: online platform 泛指任何在线服务（含购物、学习、办公等），范围更广；social media 特指以社交、内容分享为核心的平台，是 online platform 的一种

synonyms.example: The Internet has placed the sum of human knowledge at our fingertips, yet wisdom still cannot be downloaded. （议论文·科技）

synonyms.example: He met his lifelong business partner not at a conference but on a professional networking site. （读后续写·机遇）
synonyms.usage: networking site 更强调建立人脉、职业联系的功能，语气偏正式；social media 更口语、更常用，涵盖社交、娱乐、资讯等更广用途

advancedExpressions.expression: post sth on / go viral on / spread rumours on / harness the power of social media

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·社交媒体（可替换）
advancedExpressions.expression: social media ≈ online platforms ≈ social networking sites ≈ digital media
advancedExpressions.example: Teenagers today spend hours on social media / online platforms / social networking sites every single day. （同义替换练"社交媒体"）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·作主语的单复数
advancedExpressions.expression: social media 视作整体时接单数动词（media has / is）

advancedExpressions.expression: no sooner had ... posted on social media than ...

advancedExpressions.expression: social media is a double-edged sword: ... on the one hand, ... on the other

readingExamples: When I called her, she said she might not be able to make it to the cinema.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to succeed in reaching a place in time, especially when this is difficult
(2) v. to be able to be present at or attend an event
(3) v. to be successful in a career or particular activity
(4) v. to survive after a serious illness, injury or difficulty

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 赶到，及时到达(尤指困难重重时)
uncommonMeanings.example: Sprinting through the rain, Tom leapt onto the platform just as the doors closed — against all odds, he had made it. （读后续写·赶车·紧张）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 能出席，能到场
uncommonMeanings.example: I am terribly sorry that I will not be able to make it to the graduation ceremony, as my flight has been cancelled. （应用文·道歉信）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 成功，事业有成
uncommonMeanings.example: Countless young people dream of making it in the world of art, yet success rewards perseverance far more than raw talent. （议论文·成功与坚持）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (在重病/危难中)活下来,挺过来

Countless young people dream of making it in the fiercely competitive world of art, yet true success, as history teaches us, rewards perseverance far more than raw talent. （议论文·成功与坚持）
After three exhausting years of night classes, she finally made it into her dream university, and the tears in her mother's eyes said everything words could not. （读后续写·奋斗有成·情感）

idioms.example: Everyone in the village had laughed at his plan to sell handmade lanterns online, but two years later he had made it big, and the laughter turned to admiration. （读后续写·逆袭）

idioms.translation: 成败在此一举,决定成败的关键
idioms.example: This final interview would make it or break it for her — years of preparation had all narrowed down to these fifteen minutes. （读后续写·关键时刻）

collocations.phrase: make it to sth（准时到达/设法到达）
collocations.translation: 【课件】能够出席；设法及时赶到某处（义项1：succeed in reaching a place in time）
collocations.example: She made it to the airport just in time to catch her plane. 她及时赶到机场，正好赶上飞机。 （课件Reading·slide10-11·准时到达/设法到达）

collocations.phrase: make it（获得成功，事业有成）
collocations.translation: 【课件】获得成功（义项2：be successful in your career）
collocations.example: England looks less likely to make it to the finals. 英格兰队看来不太可能进入决赛了。 （课件Reading·slide10-11·获得成功）

collocations.translation: 【课件】（重病/事故后）活下来、渡过难关（义项3：survive after a serious illness or accident）
collocations.example: Frank was very ill, and the doctors didn't think he'd make it. 弗兰克病得很重，医生们认为他挺不过来了。 （课件Reading·slide10-11·渡过难关）

collocations.phrase: might not be able to make it (to the cinema)
collocations.translation: 可能来不了/赶不到（电影院）（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: When I called her, she said she might not be able to make it to the cinema. （课文原句·Amy's post）

collocations.translation: 赶到/来得及参加某处(某活动)
collocations.example: Despite the heavy snow, nearly the whole class made it to the farewell party. （读后续写·友情）
If we leave now, we should just make it on time for the opening ceremony. （应用文·活动安排）

collocations.phrase: make it in life / in one's career
collocations.translation: 在人生/事业上取得成功
collocations.example: He was determined to make it in life, to prove to his late father that his faith had not been misplaced. （读后续写·励志）
She was certain she would never make it through the final round, yet her trembling hands steadied when the music began. （读后续写·克服恐惧）

collocations.translation: 没能赶到;没能挺过来;失败
collocations.example: By the time the ambulance arrived, everyone feared the old man would not make it. （读后续写·危急）
We barely made it before the gates were locked, our chests heaving from the desperate run. （读后续写·惊险）

collocations.phrase: make it big / make it to the top
collocations.example: To make it to the top of any field, one must be willing to fall repeatedly and rise a little wiser. （议论文·成功之道）

synonyms.example: Those who succeed are rarely the most gifted, but almost always the most persistent. （议论文·坚持）
synonyms.usage: succeed 为正式书面用词，泛指各类成功，后接 in doing / in sth；make it 更口语、更生动，尤指历经艰辛后的成功或及时赶到，常独立成句（he made it）

synonyms.example: She arrived in time to catch her daughter's very first steps on stage. （读后续写·亲情）
synonyms.usage: arrive in time 仅表"及时到达"这一具体动作；make it (to) 还隐含"克服了困难才赶到"的意味，更含情绪张力

synonyms.example: The whole family kept vigil by his bed, silently willing him to pull through the long, dark night. （读后续写·亲情/坚持）
synonyms.usage: pull through 专指从重病或危机中挺过来，与 make it "活下来"义近；但 pull through 不含"赶到、成功"等其他义项，语义更窄

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·be worth doing（主动表被动）【课件slide24/27】
advancedExpressions.expression: be (well) worth doing / be worth + n. / be worth it：值得做/值得……
advancedExpressions.example: This book is well worth reading; the plan is worth a try; the holiday cost a lot, but it was worth it. 这本书很值得一读；这个计划值得一试；假期花了不少钱，但很值。 （课件slide24-27·worth doing 用主动形式表被动 doing=being done）

advancedExpressions.expression: make it to / make it on time / make it through / make it big / not make it
advancedExpressions.example: Against all odds she made it through the storm, made it to the hall on time, and one day she would make it big. （make it 多义搭配串联）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·成功办到（可替换，视语境）
advancedExpressions.expression: make it ≈ succeed（成功）/ arrive in time（及时赶到）/ pull through（渡过难关）
advancedExpressions.example: After years of struggle he finally made it / succeeded, and his sick mother, against all odds, made it / pulled through too. （按语境替换 make it）

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·be able to make it
advancedExpressions.expression: be (not) able to make it (to ...)：能/不能赶到或出席
advancedExpressions.example: She said she might not be able to make it to the cinema. （情态 might + be able to make it，委婉表"可能来不了"，即课文句式）

advancedExpressions.expression: against all odds, sb. (had) finally made it
advancedExpressions.example: Against all odds — the missed bus, the sudden downpour, the throbbing ankle — she had finally made it, collapsing breathless but triumphant against the auditorium door. （against all odds+破折号列举障碍）

advancedExpressions.expression: much to my regret, I am afraid I won't be able to make it
advancedExpressions.example: Much to my regret, I am afraid I won't be able to make it to your birthday gathering, but please know that my warmest wishes will be there in my place. （婉拒句式+情感补偿）

advancedExpressions.expression: it is not talent but perseverance that ultimately decides who makes it
advancedExpressions.example: History reminds us again and again that it is not talent but perseverance that ultimately decides who makes it and who fades into obscurity. （强调句+对比）

sentenceUpgrade.original: He ran fast and got to the station in time.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Legs burning and lungs screaming for air, he tore down the empty street, and just as hope began to slip away, he made it — the train still waiting, its doors mercifully open. （读后续写·动作+心理）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 分词独立结构(Legs burning...lungs screaming)渲染拼尽全力 + just as...制造千钧一发 + 破折号补充画面 + mercifully副词传递侥幸情绪

sentenceUpgrade.original: Many people want to be successful but few do.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Many set out with grand ambitions of making it, yet only a resolute few possess the quiet endurance to weather the years of obscurity that success invariably demands. （议论文·对比论证）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Many...yet only a few对比结构 + making it口语短语提升可读性 + weather the years比喻 + invariably副词加强论断力度

classPractice.question:
根据语境，判断下列 make it 的含义（渡过难关 / 获得成功 / 准时到达 / 设法到达 / 能够出席）：
1) Frank was very ill, and the doctors didn't think he'd make it.
2) England looks less likely to make it to the finals.
3) She made it to the airport just in time to catch her plane.
4) With blood pouring from his leg, he made it to a nearby house.
5) I can't make it to the meeting tonight, but I'll be with you in spirit.
classPractice.answer: 1) 渡过难关  2) 获得成功  3) 准时到达  4) 设法到达  5) 能够出席
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】make it 一词多义，须依语境判断；课件 slide11 原题原答案

classPractice.question:
这本书很值得一读。（worth）
This book ____ ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】be (well) worth doing "某事（很）值得做"，主动形式表被动含义（reading=being read）；课件 slide24

classPractice.question:
这个计划值得一试。（worth）
The plan ____ ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】be worth + n. "值得……"，worth 后可直接接名词 a try；课件 slide24

classPractice.question:
度假花了不少钱，但是很值。
The holiday cost a lot, but it ____ ____ ____.
classPractice.note: 【课件原题】be worth it "值得"，worth 后接代词 it；课件 slide24/27

classPractice.question:
她打电话说她可能来不了电影院了。（make）
She called to say that she might not be able to ____ ____ to the cinema.
classPractice.note: make it to + 地点 "赶到/能到某处"（课文原句）；此处指"来不了"

classPractice.question:
从 make it / succeed 中选最口语生动者：
After years of failure, he finally ____, and the whole town cheered.（历经艰辛终获成功·独立成句）
classPractice.note: make it 口语生动，尤指历经艰辛后成功，可独立成句；succeed 后常需 in doing，语气较正式

classPractice.question:
医生说他情况危急，大家都担心他挺不过来。
The doctor said it was critical, and everyone feared he would not ____ ____.
classPractice.note: not make it 在此指"(重病中)挺不过来、活不下来"；make it 一词多义，看语境判断

translation: 令人震惊的；可恶的，极坏的
original_sentence: Today, however, I received a horrible surprise.
readingExamples: Today, however, I received a horrible surprise.
definitionEn:
(1) adj. very unpleasant or shocking, causing feelings of horror, fear or disgust
(2) adj. very bad in quality or ability; extremely unpleasant to experience
(3) adj. (of a person or behaviour) unkind, unfriendly or unpleasant to deal with

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 【课件】惊恐，震惊；令人惊恐的事（horrible 的名词 horror；a horror film 恐怖片 / in horror 惊恐地 / to sb's horror 令某人惊恐的是 / fill sb with horror 使某人充满恐惧）
uncommonMeanings.example: To the captain's horror, he found that the ship was sinking, and the thought of the icy water filled every sailor with horror. （课件Reading·slide13·horror 名词多搭配合一）

posExamples.sentence: A horrible silence hung over the classroom as the teacher slowly unfolded the crumpled note, and for one dreadful moment nobody dared to breathe. （读后续写·紧张氛围）
I am writing to complain about the horrible service I received at your restaurant last Friday, which utterly ruined what should have been a joyful family celebration. （应用文·投诉信）
War is horrible not merely because of the lives it claims, but because of the enduring scars it carves into the memory of every generation that survives it. （议论文·和平主题）
When she peeled back the bandage, the horrible sight made her stomach lurch, yet she forced a steady smile so as not to frighten the injured child. （读后续写·救助·心理克制）

wordForms.adverb: horribly (adv. 可怕地,非常糟糕地)
wordForms.other: 构词法:horr-(词根,表'颤抖、恐惧')+-ible→horrible;horror(n.)→horrify(v.)→horrifying(令人恐惧的,修饰物/事)/horrified(感到恐惧的,修饰人)。辨析:horrible/horrific 都作'可怕的';-ing 形容物(a horrifying scene),-ed 形容人(a horrified look)。贴士:horror film 恐怖片;horror(n.)前不加 the 泛指'恐怖'。

collocations.translation: 【课件】义项1：causing or likely to cause horror; shocking 骇人听闻的（≈terrible, awful）
collocations.example: The nightmare was so horrible that she couldn't help screaming. 这个噩梦太可怕，她不禁尖叫起来。 （课件Reading·slide12·义项1骇人听闻的）

collocations.phrase: a horrible surprise（可恶的、糟糕的）
collocations.translation: 【课件】义项2：very unpleasant 可恶的，糟糕的
collocations.example: Today, however, I received a horrible surprise. 然而今天，我收到了一个可怕的意外。 （课件Reading·slide12·义项2糟糕的·课文原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】一部恐怖片（horror n.惊恐、震惊；令人惊恐之事）
collocations.example: They spent the rainy evening curled up watching a horror film. 他们蜷缩着度过了那个雨夜，看了一部恐怖片。 （课件Reading·slide13·horror 名词搭配）
She stepped back in horror as the shadow moved across the wall. 影子在墙上移动，她惊恐地后退。 （课件Reading·slide13·in horror 惊恐地）
To the captain's horror, he found that the ship was sinking. 令船长惊恐的是，他发现船正在下沉。 （课件Reading·slide13·to sb's horror 原句）
The thought of making a speech in front of so many people filled me with great horror. 一想到要在那么多人面前演讲，我就一阵害怕。 （课件Reading·slide13·fill sb with horror 原句）

collocations.translation: 遭遇一个可怕的意外（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Today, however, I received a horrible surprise. （课文原句）
Opening the door, she received a horrible shock: the room she had left so tidy now lay in utter chaos. （读后续写·突发情节）
A horrible feeling that something had gone wrong gnawed at him the whole way home. （读后续写·不祥预感）
I felt horrible about forgetting her birthday, and no apology seemed enough. （读后续写·愧疚）
The medicine tasted horrible, but the boy swallowed it without a word. （读后续写·坚强）
The storm had left the playground in a horrible mess. （读后续写·集体行动）
Only later did he realise the horrible mistake he had made. （读后续写·悔悟）
Despite the horrible weather, the volunteers pressed on. （读后续写·奉献）
She had been horrible to the new student all week. （读后续写·转变）

synonyms.translation: 【课件】可怕的,糟糕的（=horrible，义项1"骇人听闻的"同义）
synonyms.example: The nightmare was so terrible / horrible that she couldn't help screaming. 这个噩梦太可怕，她不禁尖叫起来。 （课件slide12·horrible=terrible=awful）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:与 horrible 几乎可互换,但 terrible 语义更广,可表示'极大的、程度极深的'(a terrible waste 极大的浪费);horrible 更侧重令人厌恶、恐惧的主观感受。句法位置相同:作定语(a terrible/horrible day)或系动词后表语(feel/look terrible)。

synonyms.translation: 【课件】糟透的,可怕的（=horrible，义项1同义）
synonyms.example: The soup tasted awful, but she finished every drop to spare the cook's feelings. （课件slide12·horrible=terrible=awful；读后续写·体贴）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:最口语、程度稍轻,日常抱怨'很糟'常用;可作程度副词 an awful lot(=非常多)。horrible 主观厌恶更强,awful 更泛用。三者(horrible/terrible/awful)均可作表语,句法位置一致,写作时替换以避免重复。

synonyms.example: A dreadful realisation dawned on her: she had left the stove burning at home. （读后续写·惊觉）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:偏书面、略正式,常修饰抽象的'处境、消息、错误';horrible 更口语，可修饰味道、天气等具体事物。

synonyms.example: The report revealed the appalling conditions the factory workers were forced to live in. （议论文·社会问题）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:程度最重,含道德上的震惊与谴责,多用于议论文揭露丑恶;horrible 语气较日常。

advancedExpressions.expression: a horrible surprise / feel horrible about sth / be horrible to sb / look·smell·taste horrible
advancedExpressions.example: I felt horrible about how horrible I had been to her. （课堂枚举:意外/愧疚/刻薄/感官四类搭配一次记牢）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·'糟糕/可怕'(可替换)
advancedExpressions.expression: horrible ↔ terrible ↔ awful ↔ dreadful ↔ appalling
advancedExpressions.example: The weather was horrible / terrible / awful that day. （功能:形容负面事物,五词均可作表语或定语,程度递增,写作换词防重复）

advancedExpressions.expression: horror(n.) → horrify(v.) → horrifying/horrified(adj.) → horribly(adv.)
advancedExpressions.example: The horrified crowd watched in horror as the horrifying scene unfolded. （名→动→形→副,一句串起词族）

advancedExpressions.expression: a horrible ... hung / settled over ...
advancedExpressions.example: A horrible stillness settled over the camp, broken only by the distant howl of the wind. （拟人营造压抑氛围）

advancedExpressions.expression: I was appalled by the horrible ... which left me ...
advancedExpressions.example: I was appalled by the horrible state of the changing rooms, which left me thoroughly disappointed. （投诉信正式措辞+which非限定从句说明后果）

advancedExpressions.expression: the ... consequences are too horrible to contemplate
advancedExpressions.example: Should we continue to ignore climate change, the consequences are too horrible to contemplate. （虚拟条件Should引导+too...to结构,警示力强）

sentenceUpgrade.original: She got a horrible surprise when she opened the letter.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The instant her eyes fell on the letter's contents, a horrible chill shot through her; the words blurred, her hands went numb, and the cheerful morning collapsed around her like shattered glass. （读后续写·心理+比喻）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: The instant引导瞬时反应 + chill shot through生理化恐惧 + 三短句并列(blurred, went numb, collapsed)节奏急促 + like shattered glass比喻情绪崩塌

sentenceUpgrade.original: The living conditions there were very horrible.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The conditions endured by these families were nothing short of horrible — cramped, damp and utterly stripped of dignity — a reality that no civilised society should tolerate. （议论文·揭露+呼吁）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: nothing short of强化程度 + 破折号三形容词排比(cramped, damp, stripped) + a reality that...同位语从句升华为道德判断

classPractice.question: The scene was so ____ (horrify) that many viewers had to look away from the screen.
classPractice.note: 考点:-ing形容词修饰事物,表'令人恐惧的';若主语是人则用horrified。

classPractice.question: 用 horrible / horrified / horror 填空:When she opened the door, a ____ smell of burning greeted her, and she stood there ____, her heart frozen with ____.
classPractice.note: 考点:horrible(adj.修饰smell) / horrified(adj.修饰人she) / horror(n.作介词with宾语),同根不同词性。

classPractice.question: 今天,然而,我收到了一个可怕的意外。(用 horrible surprise,还原课文)
classPractice.answer: Today, however, I received a horrible surprise.
classPractice.note: 考点:课文原句词块 received a horrible surprise;however作插入语用逗号隔开。

original_sentence: A classmate told me she had seen my friend chatting with another girl in a café on Saturday afternoon.
readingExamples: A classmate told me she had seen my friend chatting with another girl in a café on Saturday afternoon.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to talk in a friendly and informal way, especially about unimportant things
(2) n. a friendly informal conversation
(3) v. to exchange messages with sb in real time over the Internet
(4) n. an online real-time conversation carried out by exchanging typed messages

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (chat sb up) 与某人搭讪,套近乎(尤指出于好感)
uncommonMeanings.example: The stranger tried to chat her up at the bus stop, but she buried her face in her book, pretending not to hear a single word. （读后续写·人物·冷淡回避）

posExamples.sentence: The two old friends sat by the fire until midnight, chatting about the mischief of their boyhood, and for a few precious hours the weight of thirty years simply melted away. （读后续写·重逢·温情）
I would be grateful if you could spare me a few minutes for a friendly chat about the details of the volunteer programme. （应用文·邀请/请求）
Some argue that endless chatting on messaging apps has quietly replaced the deep, face-to-face conversations that once bound families together. （议论文·科技与沟通）
A gentle chat with the frightened new pupil did more to calm her nerves than any stern instruction ever could. （读后续写·关怀·细节）

wordForms.noun: chat / chatter (n. 唠叨,喋喋不休) / chatterbox (n. 话匣子,唠叨的人)
wordForms.other: 拼写特例:chat 为'重读闭音节+单辅音',变过去式/现在分词双写t→chatted / chatting。搭配贴士:chat 后接人用 with/to,接话题用 about;chit-chat(闲扯)、chatterbox(话匣子)为口语衍生。

idioms.example: After class, the teacher had a quiet chat with him, and something in her kind, patient tone finally coaxed the truth out of the boy. （读后续写·师生·倾诉）
The interview began with a few minutes of light chit-chat, which helped put the nervous candidate at ease. （读后续写·缓和气氛）

collocations.translation: (在咖啡馆)和某人聊天（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: A classmate told me she had seen my friend chatting with another girl in a café on Saturday afternoon. （课文原句）

collocations.phrase: chat with / to sb about sth
collocations.example: She spent the whole afternoon chatting with her grandmother about the old days. （读后续写·亲情）
They chatted about everything and nothing, and two strangers became friends. （读后续写·友谊萌芽）
Whenever you feel overwhelmed, come and have a chat with me. （应用文·安慰信）
The shy inventor was invited onto a popular chat show. （读后续写·出彩时刻）
The news broke first in the class group chat. （读后续写·信息传播）
The two pen pals had chatted online for years before they finally met. （读后续写·重逢）

collocations.translation: 喋喋不休地聊,聊个不停
collocations.example: The children chatted away happily on the long coach journey. （读后续写·天真）

synonyms.example: We need to talk seriously about what happened yesterday. （日常）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:最中性通用,可正式可随意;chat 专指轻松、随意、不涉正事的闲谈,不用于严肃谈话。句法:talk to/with sb about sth,与 chat 一致,均为不及物,后接介词。

synonyms.example: The neighbours gossiped about the newcomer for weeks, though not one of them had ever spoken to him. （读后续写·世态）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:含贬义,指议论他人隐私、说长道短;chat 为中性,单纯指友好闲聊。句法:gossip about sb/sth,不及物,写作时不可与 chat 随意互换。

synonyms.example: The two old ladies could natter for hours over a single pot of tea. （读后续写·生活气息）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:非常口语、偏英式,略带'絮叨'意味;chat 更通用、书面口语皆宜。句法:natter (away) about sth,不及物,与 chat away 结构相同。

advancedExpressions.expression: chat with/to sb about sth / have a chat / chat away / chat online / a group chat

definitionEn:

(3) n. an establishment offering a particular service alongside refreshments, e.g. an Internet café

translation: 恢复健康；恢复常态 vt. 全额收回；寻回；重新获得；恢复，重新控制
original_sentence: Instead of recovering at home, she was out having fun with someone else.
readingExamples: Instead of recovering at home, she was out having fun with someone else.
definitionEn:
(1) v. to get better after an illness, injury, shock or other difficulty; to return to a normal state
(2) v. to get back sth that was lost, stolen or taken away
(3) v. to get back the use of your senses, control, or a normal condition after losing it
(4) v. (of a market, economy, etc.) to return to a former and better state after a decline

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 寻回,找回(丢失或被盗之物);(尤指)打捞、收回【熟词僻义:不是'康复'而是'把东西找回来'】
uncommonMeanings.example: Divers worked through the night to recover the sunken cargo. （读后续写·救援·坚持）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 重新控制,恢复(镇定、意识、体力等)
uncommonMeanings.example: It took her a long moment to recover her composure before she stepped onto the stage. （读后续写·临场·心理调整）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: (市场、经济)复苏,回升到较好状态
uncommonMeanings.example: After months of decline, the market slowly began to recover. （议论文·经济）

posExamples.sentence: It was weeks before the old fisherman fully recovered from his fall, yet each morning he limped down to the shore, refusing to let the sea forget his name. （读后续写·坚韧·人物）
I am pleased to inform you that the wallet you lost at our library has been recovered and is now waiting to be collected at the front desk. （应用文·失物招领通知）
A society, much like an individual, can recover from even the gravest of setbacks, provided its people preserve their unity and their hope. （议论文·社会/复苏）
The moment the ball slipped from her grasp she froze, but she recovered in an instant, lunging sideways to snatch it back before it struck the ground. （读后续写·比赛·瞬间反应）

wordForms.noun: recovery (n. 恢复,康复,复苏,寻回) / recoverer
wordForms.adjective: recoverable (adj. 可恢复的,可收回的)
wordForms.other: 构词法:re-(词根 cover'覆盖、遮盖'加前缀 re-,原义'重新盖上'→'恢复原状')→recover。派生:recover(v.)→recovery(n.)→recoverable(adj.)。辨析:recover'恢复/找回'≠ discover'发现'≠ cover'覆盖',三词同根 cover。贴士:make a full recovery(完全康复);on the road to recovery(康复途中)。

collocations.translation: 【课件】从（疾病/痛苦）中恢复健康、恢复常态（义项1：vi. return to normal situation）
collocations.example: It can take many years to recover from the death of a loved one. 从心爱的人去世的痛苦中恢复过来可能要花很多年。 （课件Reading·slide14·vi.恢复健康·原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】义项2：vt. to get back sth that was lost/stolen 重新获得；寻回
collocations.example: Four paintings stolen from the gallery have been recovered. 从画廊被盗的四幅画已被寻回。 （课件Reading·slide14·vt.寻回·原句）

collocations.translation: 【课件】静下心来，恢复镇定（义项3：get back the use of your senses/control）
collocations.example: She seemed upset but quickly recovered herself. 她显得心烦意乱，但很快静下心来。 （课件Reading·slide15·recover oneself·原句）

collocations.phrase: make a full recovery from sth
collocations.translation: 【课件】从……完全康复（recovery n.恢复、复苏、康复）
collocations.example: My father has made a full recovery from the operation. 我父亲手术后已完全康复了。 （课件Reading·slide15·recovery·原句）

collocations.translation: 在家休养/康复（课文原句词块）
collocations.example: Instead of recovering at home, she was out having fun with someone else. （课文原句）
It took him a full year to recover from the accident. （读后续写·成长）
We all prayed she would make a speedy recovery. （读后续写·亲情·希望）
When the injured driver recovered consciousness, his first question was whether the child had been saved. （读后续写·无私）
Stumbling on the icy step, she quickly recovered her balance. （读后续写·助人）

collocations.translation: 追回被盗物品（熟词僻义:找回）
collocations.example: Thanks to a sharp-eyed neighbour, the police recovered the stolen goods within hours. （读后续写·正义得张）
After a hot meal, the exhausted hikers recovered enough strength to press on. （读后续写·登山）
Given time and sound policy, even the most battered economy can recover. （议论文·经济）

collocations.translation: 在康复的路上,渐入佳境
collocations.example: The doctor's smile told them their father was, at long last, on the road to recovery. （读后续写·转机）

synonyms.example: She spent a quiet fortnight by the sea, recuperating from months of overwork. （读后续写·休养）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:偏书面,特指'通过休息静养来康复',强调恢复过程,常搭配 recuperate from;recover 更通用,可指病愈、找回失物、恢复镇定等多义。句法:两者均为不及物,后接 from sth。

synonyms.example: The loyal dog plunged into the river to retrieve the boy's drifting hat. （读后续写·忠犬）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:仅对应 recover 的'寻回'义,强调'把某物取回来'的动作,及物,直接接 sth(retrieve the data/hat);不能表示'病愈、经济复苏'。recover 兼有'康复'与'找回'两义。

synonyms.translation: 重新获得,恢复(尤指抽象事物)
synonyms.example: Slowly, through small daily kindnesses, he regained the trust he had thrown away. （读后续写·修复关系）
synonyms.usage: 中文辨析:及物动词,强调'重新得到失去的(信心、意识、力量、信任、控制)',regain consciousness/one's strength;与 recover 的'恢复'义近,但 regain 不用于'病愈'和'找回丢失的实物'。

advancedExpressions.expression: recover from sth / recover consciousness·one's composure / recover the stolen goods / make a full recovery / on the road to recovery
advancedExpressions.example: After the crash he recovered consciousness, and within a month made a full recovery. （课堂枚举:康复、恢复意识、找回、名词短语一次记牢）

advancedExpressions.type: 同义表达群·'恢复/康复'(按义分工,部分可替换)
advancedExpressions.expression: recover(病愈/找回) ↔ recuperate(静养康复) ↔ regain(重获抽象物) ↔ retrieve(取回实物) ↔ get better(口语)

advancedExpressions.expression: slowly but surely, sb. began to recover ...
advancedExpressions.example: Slowly but surely, colour began to return to his cheeks; he was recovering at last. （slowly but surely渐进副词+colour returning具象康复）

advancedExpressions.expression: I am delighted to inform you that ... has been recovered
advancedExpressions.example: I am delighted to inform you that the camera reported missing has been recovered and returned to the lost-and-found office. （告知句式,正式且传递好消息）

advancedExpressions.expression: true strength lies not in never falling, but in the ability to recover
advancedExpressions.example: True strength lies not in never falling, but in the quiet, dogged ability to recover, to rise, and to walk on. （not...but对比+三动词递进,凸显韧性主题）

sentenceUpgrade.original: After being ill, she slowly got better.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Week by week, the roses crept back into her pale cheeks, and the girl who had lain so still now laughed once more at the sparrows outside her window — she was, at long last, recovering. （读后续写·康复+环境映衬）
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: Week by week渐进时间状语 + roses crept back隐喻气色回升 + who had lain so still定语从句对比前后 + 破折号收束点题recovering
